-2.help: Compares the two file allocation tables and produce a full diff. This can be used to check that the disk is not corrupted, and have a look to it before trying to merge it with -m.

-L.help: Same as -l, but using the cluster cluster number as source. If -d is present, deleted files will be listed.

-R.help: Reads the file starting at the cluster cluster number. If size is provied, this will only read size bytes.

-b.help: Backups your FAT tables to the backupfile file. You can specify with -t the table(s) you want to backup (0:both, 1:first, 2:sec‐ ond). You can then apply the FATs using -p.

-e.help: Display information about the entry of the path file or directory. You can edit its cluster or size reference using -c and -s.

-f.help: Walks the directories from the root (/) and try to fix unallocated files and directories FAT table.

-i.help: Display information about the FAT filesystem

-k.help: Walks the directories from the root (/) and search an entry refer‐ encing the given cluster.

-l.help: Lists the entries of the directory path If -d is present, deleted files will be listed.

-m.help: Merges the two file allocation tables. This will only keep the al‐ located entries from on or the other table.

-o.help: Search for orphaned files on the disk. This will produce a log listing files, directories and entries that are found. See -L, -R and -x to access those files and directories.

-p.help: Patch your FAT table using backupfile previously backuped file (us‐ ing -b). You can use -t to specify the table(s) you want to patch (0: both, 1:first, 2:second).

-r.help: Reads the file given by path

-s.help: specify the size of data to read from the cluster

-w.help: Writes the cluster entry in the FAT to value. You can specify the table using -t (0:both, 1:first, 2: second).

-x.help: Extract all the files to the target directory. If you provide a cluster with -c, the extract will start with the given cluster in‐ stead that the root directory. If -d is present, deleted files will be extracted.
